# fortiappseccloud_waf_template_information_leakage

Configures information leakage for one FortiAppSec Cloud WAF template using the static template endpoint `/waf/template/{template_id}/information_leakage`. This resource owns the template's module settings. To make an application inherit them, configure the matching app module resource with `template = true` and omit its `configs` block.

Declare only one `fortiappseccloud_waf_template_information_leakage` resource for a WAF template.

## Example Usage

```hcl
resource "fortiappseccloud_waf_template_information_leakage" "example" {
  template_id = fortiappseccloud_waf_template.example.template_id

  configs {
    status               = true
    action               = "deny_erase_no_log"
    cloak_error_pages    = true
    erase_http_headers   = true
    personal_info        = true
    server_info_disclose = true

    http_headers {
      item {
        header = "Server"
      }
    }

    sig_except_rules {
      item {
        sig_id   = "030000010"
        sig_name = "SQL Injection"
        cookie {
          status = true
          type   = "string"
          value  = "sessionid"
        }
        host {
          status = true
          type   = "string"
          value  = "www.example.com"
        }
        http_header {
          status = true
          type   = "string"
          value  = "X-Example"
        }
        json {
          status = true
          type   = "string"
          value  = "data"
        }
        param {
          status = true
          type   = "string"
          value  = "query"
        }
        url {
          status = true
          type   = "regex"
          value  = "^/admin"
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Argument Reference

- `template_id` (Required, Forces replacement) — WAF template ID.
- `configs` (Required) — Typed information leakage configuration. Its attributes and ownership-wrapper blocks are identical to `fortiappseccloud_waf_information_leakage` when that app resource uses `template = false`.

## Import

Import using the template ID:

```shell
terraform import fortiappseccloud_waf_template_information_leakage.example TEMPLATE_ID
```

The first read after import hydrates all supported ownership wrappers.

## Destroy Behavior
Destroy performs a fresh GET, preserves the complete response, sets `template=false` and `configs.status=false`, sends the complete PUT, and verifies the normalized GET response before Terraform removes the resource from state.
